summary: Round 4, judged from scratch. The brief is met: pan +-90 and tilt -35..+65 are swept clear, two catalog SG90s, a Camera Module 3 proxy, a captive 1/4-20 nut and a torque_tilt requirement at 2% of stall. The mechanics hold up: the tilt bracket is carried on both sides, the three FEA hot spots sit where the load enters (tilt tab screws and wall roots, horn-face hub, pan tab screws) at 1-3 MPa against a 13 MPa limit, and all hex-key paths are straight. The round-3 major (no electrical system) is fixed: the 5 V supply, jack, Pi Zero 2 W and four wiring runs are rated and routed, and power_budget is 14%. Only minor items remain, mostly estimated horn dimensions and thin tolerances that need a test print.

findings.issue: The 21T aluminium horn bolt circle (12 mm), M2 thread and 4 mm hub depth are catalog ESTIMATES (A3). The SG90 tab-hole position and shaft offset were scaled from a drawing. A wrong horn puts four bolt holes in the bracket and yoke in the wrong place.
findings.fix: Measure the purchased horns and servos before printing. Print the base first as a test-fit coupon, and print the bracket's horn plate before the full part. Update the catalog if the numbers differ.

findings.issue: The pivot axial gap is 0.9 mm against a 0.8 mm cam_clear requirement, so only 0.1 mm of margin. Shrinkage or elephant's foot on the yoke -Y wall and the knuckle could bind the tilt, and the pivot screw is meant to be backed off 1/8 turn.
findings.fix: After the first print, check the tilt by hand. If it is tight, face the knuckle or wall with a 0.2 mm shim or sand the faces. Consider 1.0 mm (the param max) as the default.

findings.issue: The WIRING steps say to cut and solder jack -> servo. An SG90 ships with its own 3-pin JR lead, and splitting power and signal as separate 2-conductor runs implies cutting that lead. Nothing specifies the connector for the 300 mm servo extensions, or that power and signal rejoin into one 3-pin plug. Wire mass is not counted in the 59.3 g head mass either (about 1 g, negligible).
findings.fix: State in WIRING/BOM that the runs are two 300 mm 3-pin servo extensions with their pins split at the supply end (red/brown to the jack, orange to the Pi GPIO). Add the 3-pin extension cable to bom_extra.

findings.issue: The Pi's 3.3 V GPIO drives the SG90 signal pin directly. This usually works, but there is no series resistor, and the common GND between the Pi USB supply and the servo supply is only a note. A missed ground tie gives twitching servos.
findings.fix: Add a 330 ohm to 1 kohm series resistor on each signal line and a bolded common-ground step to ASSEMBLY/WIRING. Keep the 470-1000 uF cap at the jack as already specified.

findings.issue: 3.5% of the surface is flagged as needing support: the 45-degree and teardrop faces, plus the roofs of the 2.4 mm horizontal key-access holes and the M3 knuckle pilot. The key-access holes are tiny and are likely to print with sag.
findings.fix: Check the sliced preview for the key-access holes and clean them with a 2.4 mm drill if needed. No geometry change required.

findings.issue: Load axis Z runs across layers on all three parts. FEA proves SF 3 against the Z strength with large margin (peaks 1.6, 3.9 and 3.6 MPa against 13 MPa). The yoke wall roots and the tilt tab pilots still have the weakest layer orientation, and the printed M2 pilots wear (already noted in section 10).
findings.fix: Print at 100% on the yoke walls, or at 5+ perimeters. Treat the tab screws as service-limited and re-tap or fit M2 heat-set inserts if they wear.

findings.issue: Several items are unpriced (servos, PSU, jack, Pi, camera, FPC, capacitor, USB supply). The horn price is $14.98 each, close to half the build cost, for parts whose geometry is estimated.
findings.fix: Add prices, and confirm the horn geometry before buying two of them.
